beats.title: Mendel Publishes Pea Experiments
beats.description: A monk in Brno reported that traits in garden peas pass down in predictable ratios, laying the groundwork for genetics.
beats.why_in: birth of the laws of heredity

beats.title: Miescher Isolates Nuclein
beats.description: A Swiss chemist extracted a phosphorus-rich substance from the nuclei of white blood cells, the first isolation of DNA.

beats.title: Flemming Watches Chromosomes Divide
beats.description: A German biologist described in detail how threadlike bodies in the nucleus split during cell division.

beats.title: Chromosomes Get Their Name
beats.description: An anatomist proposed the word for the dye-absorbing threads inside the nucleus that carry hereditary material.

beats.title: Weismann Proposes the Germ Plasm
beats.description: A German biologist argued that heredity passes only through reproductive cells, separate from the rest of the body.

beats.title: Mendel's Work Is Rediscovered
beats.description: Three botanists independently unearthed the forgotten pea experiments and confirmed the rules of inheritance.

beats.title: Chromosomes Linked to Heredity
beats.description: Two biologists separately proposed that Mendel's factors are carried on chromosomes, which pair up and separate.

beats.title: The Word Gene Is Coined
beats.description: A Danish botanist introduced a short name for the units of heredity, giving a new science its central term.

beats.title: Morgan's Fruit Flies Reveal Linkage
beats.description: A white-eyed mutant fly in a Columbia lab showed that a trait is tied to a specific chromosome, starting gene mapping.

beats.title: First Genetic Map Is Drawn
beats.description: A student of Morgan's arranged genes in a line along a fruit fly chromosome by how often they were inherited together.

beats.title: X-rays Shown to Cause Mutations
beats.description: Hermann Muller bombarded fruit flies with radiation and proved that it dramatically increased heritable genetic changes.

beats.title: Griffith's Transforming Principle
beats.description: Harmless bacteria turned deadly after mixing with dead virulent ones, hinting at a heritable substance passing between cells.

beats.title: Crossing Over Seen in Chromosomes
beats.description: Barbara McClintock and a student showed that chromosomes physically swap segments, explaining how traits get shuffled.

beats.title: One Gene, One Enzyme
beats.description: Experiments on bread mould showed that each gene directs the making of one specific protein enzyme.

beats.title: Avery Shows DNA Carries Heredity
beats.description: Researchers at the Rockefeller Institute identified DNA, not protein, as the substance that transforms bacteria.

beats.title: Bacteria Found Swapping Genes
beats.description: Lederberg and Tatum showed that bacteria can exchange genetic material, opening the door to bacterial genetics.

beats.title: Hershey-Chase Blender Experiment
beats.description: Viruses labelled with radioactive tags proved that DNA, not protein, enters a bacterium to direct new viruses.

beats.title: Watson and Crick's Double Helix
beats.description: Two Cambridge researchers proposed the twisted-ladder structure of DNA, showing how genetic information could be copied.

beats.title: Humans Counted at 46 Chromosomes
beats.description: Better lab methods finally showed that human cells hold 46 chromosomes, not the 48 long assumed.

beats.title: The Genetic Code Is Cracked
beats.description: Researchers completed the dictionary linking each three-letter DNA codon to the amino acid it specifies.

beats.title: First Useful Restriction Enzyme
beats.description: Scientists at Johns Hopkins found an enzyme that cuts DNA at a specific sequence, a molecular pair of scissors.

beats.title: Recombinant DNA Is Created
beats.description: Cohen and Boyer spliced a gene from one organism into a bacterium, launching genetic engineering.

beats.title: Sanger Sequences DNA
beats.description: Frederick Sanger published a fast chain-termination method for reading the order of letters in DNA.

beats.title: PCR Is Invented
beats.description: Kary Mullis conceived a way to copy a tiny DNA fragment into billions of copies in a test tube.

beats.title: DNA Fingerprinting Is Invented
beats.description: Alec Jeffreys at Leicester discovered that each person's DNA pattern is unique, creating forensic genetic identification.

beats.title: Human Genome Project Launches
beats.description: An international effort began to map and sequence all the genes of the human species.
beats.note: Also the year of the first gene therapy trial.

beats.title: Dolly the Sheep Is Born
beats.description: Scientists in Scotland produced a lamb cloned from an adult cell, proving a mature cell's genes could restart development.

beats.title: Draft Human Genome Published
beats.description: Rival public and private teams released their first full drafts of the roughly three billion letters of human DNA.

beats.title: Human Genome Project Completed
beats.description: The international project announced it had finished sequencing the human genome, ahead of schedule.

beats.title: Yamanaka Makes Stem Cells From Skin
beats.description: Adding just four genes turned ordinary mouse skin cells back into cells able to become any tissue.

beats.title: CRISPR Gene Editing Demonstrated
beats.description: Doudna and Charpentier showed a bacterial defence system could be programmed to cut DNA at any chosen spot.

beats.title: Gene-Edited Babies Announced
beats.description: A Chinese scientist claimed to have created twin girls with edited embryo DNA, prompting worldwide condemnation.

beats.title: First CRISPR Therapy Approved
beats.description: Regulators cleared a treatment for sickle cell disease that edits patients' own cells, the first licensed use of CRISPR.

beats.title: Custom Base Editing Treats a Baby
beats.description: Doctors designed a bespoke gene-editing therapy in months to treat an infant with a rare metabolic disorder.
